Spinning a new tale 🧶\
\
Cotton has been a part of our everyday lives for centuries, so how do we use recycled cotton while keeping the soft, high-quality feel?\
\
Our first step was to look at what already exists - production leftovers like small pieces, yarn ends and trimmings. By using these, we can save on resources and prevent waste.\
\
Then, through a series of careful balancing and testing at our IKEA Test and Development Lab in Älmhult, we blend recycled cotton with virgin cotton and test it in the same way we test virgin cotton to achieve the softness and quality of our new ÄNGSLILJA bed linen, which is made with at least 50% recycled cotton sourced from textile production waste.\
\
Tap the link in bio to learn more!\

For over 30 years, our iconic FRAKTA bag has been one of the most used bags in the world—whether for shopping, moving, doing the laundry, or going to the beach.\
 \
The name means ’to freight’ in Swedish; this bag was originally designed for IKEA customers to carry their new purchases home.\
 \
Over the years, millions of people have come up with imaginative and alternative ways to use FRAKTA, and we’ve also had various collaborations to reimagine it. Swipe to see how it’s been reimagined throughout the years.\
 \
#FRAKTA\
\
A limited edition from the #YPPERLIG collection with designer duo Mette and Rolf Hay, 2016\
\
Created in association with Craig Redman for the #FÖRNYAD collection, the FRAKTA was given a fun and bright pattern\
\
Designer Virgil Abloh created his version for the #MARKERAD collection in 2019\
\
In 2021, we teamed up with designer Zandra Rhodes on the #KARISMATISK collection where she added her playful twist and cheerful colour palette!\
\
In 2022, we collaborated with Swedish House Mafia to create a FRAKTA for the #OBEGRÄNSAD collection

More than just a shopping bag 💙\
\
We’ve updated one of our most loved and iconic products - the FRAKTA carrier bag. Originally designed in 1996 as a practical way for our customers to bring their purchases home, it has since evolved into one of the most recognised symbols and a versatile solution for countless everyday tasks at home and beyond.\
\
As one of our most loved and iconic products, we wanted to secure the FRAKTA bag’s future, so we spent several years finding innovative solutions that allowed us to make it with a high share of recycled materials without compromising on what makes this bag unique.\
\
The bags in 36-litre and 71-litre sizes are now made with a minimum of 90% recycled materials, of which at least 70% comes from packaging waste from the food and plastic industries.\
\
Learn more about this journey at 🔗 in bio!
